list.doc: Personal Calendar aggregated read. Returns one flat, time-sorted list of the caller's Tasks and Meetings across every workspace they belong to, plus their personal-hub items. READ-ONLY: the Calendar writes through the owning service (task.update / task.update_status / room.book / room.update) addressed with each row's own hub_id, so ACL and audit stay identical to editing the item in its folder. Meetings come from one indexed read of the global yp.meeting_schedule index (organizer or attendee); tasks come from task_list_range run against the caller's own database plus each workspace database.

from.doc: Inclusive start of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Rejected with INVALID_DATE_RANGE if malformed.

to.doc: Inclusive end of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Must not precede `from`.

kinds.doc: Restrict to 'task' and/or 'meeting'. Omit for both.

returns.doc: Time-sorted calendar rows. Meetings carry epoch stime/etime; tasks are all-day and carry due_date (plus start_date when the task spans a range).

id.doc: Record id in its own store: task id, or the meeting node id

hub_id.doc: Owning hub. REQUIRED by the client: every write goes back to this hub, and 'Open in folder' cannot be built without it

nid.doc: Owning folder node for a task (null at workspace root); the meeting node for a meeting

origin_name.doc: Folder name for a folder task, workspace name for a workspace meeting or a root task, null when personal

description.doc: Task description, or the meeting agenda

due_date.doc: Tasks only, YYYY-MM-DD. Tasks are all-day items

start_date.doc: Tasks only. Set when the task spans start_date..due_date

stime.doc: Meetings only. UNIX-epoch seconds — the canonical meeting time

status.doc: Column key: a built-in (todo|in_progress|to_review|complete) or a custom task_column id

status_label.doc: Resolved column name, or null when the scope's columns were never seeded — a custom column belongs to a folder the client never loads, so the label has to travel with the row

status_theme.doc: Resolved column palette key, same rationale as status_label

can_write.doc: 1 when the caller may edit this row from the Calendar. Folder-owned rows answer 0: they are edited in their folder. Meetings answer 1 only for the creator, matching room.update's creator-only rule

recur.doc: Recurrence rule {freq, until} or null. Occurrences are expanded CLIENT-side, per the room service's stated contract

errors.message: Every task source failed to answer — the calendar could not be read. Distinct from an empty calendar, which returns an empty list.
